paragraphs: Nearest-neighbor search becomes expensive when the most accurate way to compare two items requires substantial computation. This paper studies a setting with two distance measures: an expensive measure that defines the desired answers and a cheaper, less accurate proxy. Its goal is to obtain accurate search results while limiting evaluations of both measures.

The framework builds its search data structures using only the cheaper proxy. At query time, it uses the two measures to approach the accuracy defined by the expensive one. The theoretical analysis covers DiskANN and Cover Tree. If the proxy approximates the expensive metric within a bounded factor, the resulting structures can provide arbitrarily good approximation guarantees relative to the expensive metric.

Experiments apply the framework to text retrieval, where different machine-learning models supply comparisons at very different computational costs. On almost all large BEIR datasets examined, the method achieves a better accuracy–efficiency balance than alternatives including retrieve-then-rerank. The contribution connects a conditional search guarantee with a practical way to spend expensive comparisons more effectively.
icml-2026-a-bi-metric-framework-for-effi.tldr: A two-metric search framework builds indexes with cheap comparisons while selectively using expensive comparisons to improve retrieval accuracy.

paragraphs: Chain of thought makes intermediate reasoning explicit by generating tokens. Latent thought instead carries out intermediate computation in a continuous internal representation. Both approaches give a model additional rounds of computation, but the paper asks whether their different representations create meaningful differences in what that computation can efficiently accomplish.

The authors provide a formal comparison showing that latent thought permits efficient parallel computation, whereas chain-of-thought generation is inherently sequential. This separates the capabilities of the two approaches rather than treating them as interchangeable ways to extend reasoning. The analysis also identifies a capability in the other direction: chain of thought can perform approximate counting through stochastic decoding, connecting its computational behavior to the randomness of generated tokens.

These results offer guidance about matching a reasoning approach to a task's computational structure. In particular, they help distinguish settings suited to parallel computation from those where depth-driven recursion is more appropriate. The contribution is a theoretical account of complementary capabilities, providing a basis for choosing between explicit token-based reasoning and computation within latent representations.
icml-2026-a-formal-comparison-between-ch.tldr: A formal analysis distinguishes latent thought's efficient parallel computation from chain of thought's sequential reasoning and stochastic approximate counting.

paragraphs: When open-ended responses have no reference answers, evaluators often ask language models to judge competing outputs. Those judges differ in reliability. Treating their decisions as equally informative can distort a leaderboard and its uncertainty estimates; collecting more comparisons can then increase confidence in an incorrect ranking.

This paper extends the Bradley-Terry-Luce model for pairwise comparisons with a separate discrimination parameter for each judge. The framework jointly estimates the underlying quality of evaluated models and the reliability of judges without reference labels. It establishes that these quantities are identifiable after natural normalizations, and proves consistency and asymptotic normality for its maximum-likelihood estimator.

Those statistical results support confidence intervals for quality differences and comparisons between ranks, making uncertainty part of the ranking procedure. Across public benchmarks and a newly collected dataset, the method agrees better with human preferences, uses comparison data more efficiently than unweighted baselines, and produces calibrated uncertainty estimates. The findings show why modeling who makes a judgment can matter alongside collecting the judgment itself.
icml-2026-a-judge-aware-ranking-framewor.tldr: Jointly estimating judge reliability and model quality improves reference-free LLM rankings and their uncertainty estimates.

paragraphs: Multi-agent language-model systems make many model calls, and how those calls are scheduled affects accuracy, latency, and cost. This paper distinguishes two ways to run work in parallel. Replica Parallelism explores several complete solutions to the same task. Structural Parallelism decomposes one solution into parts that can execute concurrently.

The proposed TIPEX framework places both forms of parallelism within a shared execution model. This makes their combinations and configuration choices controllable and systematically comparable. The distinction matters because attempting more complete solutions and accelerating work inside a solution allocate computation differently, even though both involve simultaneous model activity.

Experiments on GAIA show that parallel execution can improve accuracy and reduce end-to-end latency while increasing token consumption. The two forms of parallelism have complementary effects across task complexities, with intermediate-difficulty tasks benefiting most from coordination. More aggressive parallelism does not necessarily improve performance. The results therefore frame scheduling as a tradeoff among solution quality, elapsed time, and token use, with the best coordination depending on task difficulty.
icml-2026-a-two-tier-perspective-on-infe.tldr: TIPEX coordinates parallel solution attempts and parallel subtasks, revealing accuracy and latency gains that come with higher token use.

paragraphs: Creative writing and open-ended instruction following have several dimensions of quality that a single reward score may poorly capture. Rubric-ARM addresses this problem by learning both the evaluation criteria and the judge that applies them. Preference feedback supplies the learning signal in domains where responses cannot simply be checked against a verifiable answer.

The framework treats generating a rubric as an internal action whose usefulness is measured by judgment accuracy. Rubrics therefore become part of the optimization process, rather than a fixed input to evaluation. The rubric generator and judge train through alternating reinforcement-learning updates. This schedule addresses the moving-target problem created when both components change simultaneously, and the paper's theoretical analysis shows how it reduces gradient variance.

Experiments report state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated baselines on multiple benchmarks. The learned reward modeling also improves downstream policy alignment in both offline and online reinforcement learning. These findings suggest that adapting evaluation criteria together with the evaluator can produce feedback that better guides subsequent model training.
icml-2026-alternating-reinforcement-lear.tldr: Rubric-ARM alternates training a rubric generator and a judge to improve preference judgments and downstream language-model alignment.

paragraphs: Policy mirror descent improves a reinforcement-learning policy through updates constrained by how far they move from a reference policy. Its ideal update requires estimating a partition function, which is difficult with limited sampled responses and a language model's enormous action space. This paper studies what happens when that difficult quantity is approximated.

The analyzed algorithm, PMD-mean, replaces the log-partition term with the sampling policy's mean reward and fits updates in log-probability space. The authors characterize its population solution and show that this substitution introduces an adaptive mixture of KL and chi-squared regularization. The additional term restrains large probability changes, yielding more conservative updates when expected rewards are low and greater robustness to finite-sample estimation errors.

Math-reasoning experiments show improved stability and competitive performance when training uses stale rollouts, meaning samples generated by an earlier policy. Larger rollout batches also support higher throughput. The central insight is that a practical approximation changes the update's regularization in a structured way, helping explain its observed training behavior.
icml-2026-approximation-of-log-partition.tldr: PMD-mean's partition-function approximation implicitly adds adaptive regularization that helps explain its conservative, stable policy updates.

paragraphs: Image-editing agents can translate broad instructions into sequences of tool operations, making their actions easier to control and inspect. Training them is harder when human feedback is sparse. Dense substitute rewards can favor tiny, numerically detectable edits that barely change perceived quality, directing learning toward the scoring mechanism instead of meaningful visual improvement.

B-Spar combines three mechanisms to address this problem. Prior-guided trajectory sampling reduces inefficient exploration of editing sequences. Bayesian reward modeling turns sparse binary feedback into a denser, more stable training signal. Anchor-regularized policy optimization then guides updates toward high-reward behavior while preventing the policy from collapsing too early into a narrow set of choices.

On public benchmarks, the authors report better perceptual quality and metric alignment, stable training, and competitive inference efficiency against strong prompt-based and training-based alternatives. They report perceptual-quality improvements exceeding 95% over AIGC-based baselines and approximately 33.5% over the state of the art. The findings support improving the reward signal itself as a route to more perceptually meaningful retouching.
icml-2026-b-spar-bayesian-sparse-reward-.tldr: B-Spar combines Bayesian reward modeling, guided exploration, and regularized updates to train image-retouching agents from sparse feedback.

paragraphs: Incomplete multi-view clustering seeks shared groups when each item may be observed through only some of its available views. Variational methods can handle missing views without filling them in, but commonly assume that views are conditionally independent. That assumption can leave structured relationships between views outside the model.

This paper introduces a variational framework with a learnable cross-view correlation structure. It estimates relationships through the covariance of posterior estimation errors, allowing the model to represent how errors across views vary together. A normalized Cholesky decomposition parameterizes the correlation matrix, keeping it positive definite. The correlations and the rest of the model are learned jointly through one variational objective.

Experiments on multiple incomplete multi-view clustering benchmarks show consistent improvements over state-of-the-art approaches across a wide range of missing-view settings. The findings support explicitly adapting to dependencies between views when discovering shared clusters. The technical contribution connects that flexibility with a constrained matrix representation that keeps correlation learning valid and supports efficient joint training.
icml-2026-beyond-independence-learning-c.tldr: Learning correlations between partially observed views improves variational clustering across the evaluated missing-data settings.

paragraphs: Synchronous reinforcement learning can leave fast GPUs idle while slower workers finish generating responses. These waiting periods become a substantial bottleneck for long-context language-model training. BubbleSpec uses those idle windows to prepare useful work for later training steps while retaining the algorithm's strict synchronization and mathematical exactness.

Faster workers pre-generate prospective rollout results during the wait. Those results become drafts for speculative decoding in subsequent steps, reducing the decoding work needed then. The framework turns uneven completion times into an opportunity for preparation. Unlike speculative methods that depend on similarity with historical epochs or require warm-up, it is designed to accelerate training immediately and without depending on dataset size.

Evaluations report approximately 50% fewer decoding steps and rollout throughput improvements of up to 1.8 times. The framework also supports different reinforcement-learning systems and strategies because it preserves synchronous behavior. Its practical significance is the ability to recover value from otherwise idle hardware time while keeping the training procedure's synchronization requirements intact.
icml-2026-bubblespec-turning-long-tail-b.tldr: BubbleSpec uses idle GPU time to draft future rollouts, accelerating decoding while preserving exact synchronous reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Generating several reasoning attempts can improve a model's answers, but repeated sampling may spend substantial effort on redundant paths. Decoding Tree Sketching, or DTS, organizes that exploration around a branching structure. Its goal is to use parallel reasoning more effectively by exploring meaningful alternatives and selecting promising trajectories during generation.

DTS sketches a backbone tree by selectively branching at decision tokens. This creates structured alternatives within the reasoning process. For selection, it uses an observed negative relationship between trajectory length and accuracy to motivate early termination, prioritizing shorter, reliable trajectories. The framework is designed as a plug-and-play decoding method, making the organization of inference the main intervention.

Experiments across four large reasoning models and datasets report average accuracy improvements of 14% and reductions in repetitive generation of 8%. The authors also report cases where smaller models outperform models ten times their size. These results show the potential of better exploration and selection to improve reasoning performance, rather than relying solely on additional sampled trajectories.
icml-2026-dts-enhancing-large-reasoning-.tldr: DTS branches selectively through reasoning paths and terminates trajectories early to improve accuracy and reduce repetitive generation.

paragraphs: Diffusion-model caching saves computation by reusing or forecasting intermediate features. Fixed forecasting formulas can fit poorly when feature dynamics differ across layers and change over time. EigenCache addresses this with a training-free approach that learns temporal covariance patterns from a small calibration set and uses them to forecast cached features.

The method represents feature trajectories as time-indexed stochastic processes and estimates a temporal kernel for each layer. Under its scalar temporal-kernel approximation, the Gaussian-process posterior mean minimizes risk among scalar-weighted linear predictors. With the additional assumption of joint Gaussianity, it is also the minimum mean-squared-error estimator. These qualifications define the scope of its optimality claim.

The same formulation supplies a posterior-variance proxy for uncertainty. EigenCache uses it to choose denoising timesteps for fresh computation through a log-determinant information objective with a near-optimal greedy solution. Across image and video models, multiple architectures, and LoRA adaptations, experiments show a strong balance between speed and fidelity. Forecasting and computation placement are thus guided by a shared model of temporal uncertainty.
icml-2026-eigencache-rethinking-diffusio.tldr: EigenCache uses learned temporal covariance and uncertainty estimates to forecast diffusion features and choose when fresh computation is most useful.

paragraphs: This paper studies privacy-preserving optimization problems in which one set of variables is minimized while another is maximized. It seeks approximate second-order stationary points, a stronger local condition than merely making the gradient small. The work treats both empirical objectives built from a dataset and population objectives representing the underlying data distribution.

The proposed algorithm uses only first-order information. It combines nested gradient descent and ascent, SPIDER-style variance reduction, and Gaussian perturbations for differential privacy. Its analysis groups iterations into blocks to control accumulated sampling variance and privacy noise, avoiding a direct accumulation across the entire iteration horizon.

Under smoothness, Hessian-Lipschitzness, and strong concavity assumptions, the authors establish high-probability second-order stationarity guarantees. The empirical accuracy parameter scales as (√d/(nε))^(2/3), while the population rate includes n^(-1/3) plus (√d/(nε))^(1/2), where d, n, and ε represent dimension, sample size, and privacy level. These rates match the best known private first-order stationarity rates, showing that the stronger local guarantee is attainable at those accuracy scales in the analyzed setting.
icml-2026-finding-differentially-private.tldr: A first-order private minimax algorithm achieves conditional second-order stationarity guarantees matching the best known private first-order accuracy rates.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning can change an encoder's internal representations and the labels used by its downstream application. That makes ownership fingerprints tied to predetermined examples and labels fragile. This paper develops a fingerprinting approach intended to verify ownership through black-box access to output labels, without requiring knowledge of the downstream task.

The method uses Adversarial Shifting to construct stable clusters of fingerprint inputs in the encoder's latent space. Its verification signal comes from consistency among cluster outputs. By relying on this consistency, the approach is designed to remain effective when the downstream task or label mapping changes, addressing the mismatch that undermines fingerprints based on fixed labels.

Experiments across downstream tasks and different numbers of categories report superior robustness and stealthiness. These findings support the use of cluster-level output consistency as a practical ownership signal for valuable pretrained encoders. The central contribution is a way to carry a recognizable fingerprint through adaptation while requiring only the limited information available from label-only queries.
icml-2026-fingerprinting-pre-trained-enc.tldr: Adversarial Shifting creates fingerprint clusters whose output consistency supports label-only encoder ownership verification after downstream fine-tuning.

paragraphs: An agent can receive language about its behavior even when the reward it should optimize is hidden. This paper formalizes that interactive learning problem and gives sufficient assumptions under which learning is possible. Its focus is understanding what information feedback must provide and how that information affects the difficulty of learning.

The authors introduce transfer eluder dimension as a measure of problem complexity. It captures the role of information in feedback and enters the performance guarantees for HELiX, their sequential learning algorithm. HELiX has a no-regret guarantee, connecting its accumulated decision quality to the structure of the language-feedback problem.

The analysis identifies cases where rich language feedback enables learning exponentially faster than reward feedback. This is a separation for particular cases, rather than a claim that all verbal feedback provides that advantage. Across several empirical domains, HELiX also performs well where repeated LLM prompting is unreliable. Together, the theory and experiments present language feedback as information that an interactive algorithm can systematically use.
icml-2026-formalizing-learning-from-lang.tldr: The paper formalizes learning from language feedback and introduces HELiX, with guarantees tied to how informative that feedback is.

paragraphs: Recovering hidden sources from mixed measurements is often approached by assuming the sources are independent or uncorrelated. This paper allows dependent latent components and instead draws information from multiple data domains. Its setting keeps the underlying latent distribution the same across domains while allowing each domain to scale the components differently.

Those changing scales provide the variation needed to separate the components. Under sufficient domain variability, the authors show that both latent variables and mixing functions can be identified using second-order statistics alone. The result makes the cross-domain structure central: dependence among sources is permitted, while the shared latent distribution and domain-specific scaling supply the identifying assumptions.

The proposed Multi-Domain Covariance Matching algorithm, MuDo-CoM, generalizes earlier joint-diagonalization methods and is validated on simulations and a real fMRI dataset. The formulation can represent measurements from different sensors, laboratories, experimental conditions, or subjects when they fit its assumptions. It provides a route to recovering individual dependent components by using structured changes across domains.
icml-2026-identifying-dependent-componen.tldr: MuDo-CoM uses domain-specific scaling differences to identify dependent latent components from covariance information under sufficient domain variability.

paragraphs: Autoregressive video generation can be slowed by repeated, sequential denoising. Reusing cached computations helps, but skipping updates for entire video chunks overlooks differences within a frame. Fast-moving pixels need more updates to avoid accumulating errors, whereas relatively static pixels can tolerate more reuse.

MotionCache connects cache errors to instability in residuals and uses differences between frames as an inexpensive indicator of local motion. It starts with a warm-up phase that establishes semantic coherence, then adjusts update frequencies for individual tokens according to motion. This coarse-to-fine procedure directs fresh computation toward changing content while reusing more work in stable regions.

On SkyReels-V2, the authors report a 6.28-times speedup with a 1% decrease in VBench. On MAGI-1, they report a 1.64-times speedup with a 0.01% decrease. These results demonstrate substantial acceleration with small measured quality reductions in the tested models. The contribution is a finer-grained way to allocate denoising effort using motion information already reflected in neighboring frames.
icml-2026-motion-aware-caching-for-effic.tldr: MotionCache accelerates video generation by reusing more computation in static regions and updating moving regions more frequently.

paragraphs: Forecasting several interacting systems requires predictions that are individually useful and mutually coordinated. Equilibrium State Estimation, or ESE, addresses this by forecasting all systems in one pass. The setting includes problems such as currency exchange and disease spread, where predicting each system separately can create substantial computational work.

ESE first estimates an equilibrium across the systems. It then uses the difference between their current state and that estimated equilibrium to generate coordinated forecasts. This shared estimation step provides a common basis for prediction. The framework can also integrate with conventional predictors, combining their predictive capability with its simultaneous forecasting procedure.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets report accuracy at least matching state-of-the-art methods alongside substantially faster execution. Integration with conventional predictors delivers reported speedups of 10–70 times. The method has linear-time complexity as the number of systems grows and remains accurate under the tested perturbations. These findings support equilibrium-based coordination as a scalable approach to forecasting multiple interacting processes.
icml-2026-once-for-all-scalable-simultan.tldr: ESE uses an estimated shared equilibrium to forecast interacting systems together, achieving comparable accuracy with substantial reported speedups.

paragraphs: Masked diffusion language models generate text by repeatedly revealing hidden tokens. The order of those reveals affects output quality, yet schedules are often chosen by heuristics. This paper turns schedule selection into a learning problem, asking which sequence of token decisions best suits the model's own predictive behavior.

The authors derive a tractable upper bound on decoding mismatch measured by KL divergence, with tightness under sufficient model expressivity. The bound yields a dense reward over ordered decoding paths. Self-Aware Scheduling uses this reward to train a lightweight scheduling policy with Group Relative Policy Optimization while keeping the denoiser frozen. It supports sequential and semi-autoregressive decoding.

On Sudoku with a 1B model, accuracy rises from 82.0% with the best heuristic to 91.8%; additional fine-tuning along learned paths reaches 97.9%. On LLaDA-8B, full-diffusion GSM8K pass@1 improves from 64% to 76%, and MBPP from 39.5% to 41%. The results show that learning when to reveal tokens can improve generation before changing the underlying denoiser.
icml-2026-scheduling-thoughts-learning-t.tldr: Self-Aware Scheduling learns token-reveal orders that improve masked diffusion models using a theoretically motivated reward.

paragraphs: Reinforcement-learning agents in open 3D worlds must reason about large, changing environments and adversarial opponents. Predicting future visual states can help, but errors can accumulate across prediction steps. ResDreamer focuses on learning representations that carry useful task information, with photorealistic reconstruction treated as secondary to that reasoning role.

Its world model has a hierarchy in which each higher layer learns to reconstruct the residuals left by the layer below. This gives higher levels a learning signal based on what lower levels have not captured. The resulting residual representations modulate lower-level predictions, supporting progressively richer abstractions of world dynamics through purely self-supervised training.

The architecture's communication cost between levels grows linearly, providing a way to expand the hierarchy without an accompanying explosion in cross-layer communication. Experiments report state-of-the-art sample efficiency and parameter efficiency. These findings support hierarchical residual modeling as a scalable route to visual foresight, with useful reasoning representations learned from the prediction process itself rather than supplied through domain-specific guidance.
icml-2026-self-supervised-hierarchical-v.tldr: ResDreamer learns hierarchical residual world models that improve the reported sample and parameter efficiency of visual reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Reasoning in a compact visual latent space can avoid explicitly generating intermediate images, but existing representations often emphasize appearance over abstract meaning. Semantic-Enriched Latent Visual Reasoning, or SLVR, adds attribute-level information so that the internal representation carries more of the semantics needed to answer questions about an image region.

The first training stage uses a semantic attribute extraction head to convert regional visual evidence into semantic latents that complement low-level features. The second stage applies Multi-query Group Relative Policy Optimization to several questions about the same region. It uses the premise that intrinsic region attributes should stay consistent across questions, constraining attribute variation while preserving answer correctness.

The authors construct SLV-Set with approximately 400,000 region-level attribute annotations and 800,000 multi-query question-answering samples. They also introduce SV-QA to evaluate reasoning under semantic variation. Experiments report improved robustness and semantic consistency. The approach ties richer representations to a training objective that encourages the same visual region to retain coherent attributes across different queries.
icml-2026-semantic-enriched-latent-visua.tldr: SLVR adds semantic attributes to visual latents and trains across related questions to improve reasoning robustness and consistency.

paragraphs: Researchers may want confidence bounds for a combined effect after choosing a subset of results from observed data. This paper studies simultaneous bounds over downward-closed families of subsets of independent statistical tests. Such families retain all smaller subsets of an allowed set, defining which aggregated effects receive protection.

The procedure uses bootstrap calibration of the largest normalized aggregate across the relevant family. That maximization is a nonlinear combinatorial problem, so the authors reformulate it as a weighted densest-subgraph problem and derive exact linear and mixed-integer linear programs. They also develop a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme using the objective's rank-one structure to handle large families.

The statistical analysis provides finite-sample coverage with a lighter dependence on family size than high-dimensional central limit theorems offer. Targeting the relevant subsets also yields tighter bounds than methods protecting all linear contrasts. Synthetic and real machine-learning applications illustrate the approach. Its contribution joins computational optimization with uncertainty guarantees that remain valid when the reported subset is selected after seeing the data.
icml-2026-simultaneous-confidence-bounds.tldr: Subset optimization enables tighter simultaneous confidence bounds for aggregated effects selected after observing independent test results.

paragraphs: Non-smooth operations such as ReLU and quantization create locations where nearby gradient signals can conflict. The paper connects these conflicts to gradient chattering: large oscillations that interfere with optimization. Singularity-aware Adam, or S-Adam, adjusts update sizes according to the instability of the local geometry.

Its Local Geometric Instability metric estimates the diameter of the Clarke subdifferential, which describes generalized gradient possibilities at a non-smooth point. The estimate comes from the variance of randomized directional derivatives. An exponential damping factor slows updates in regions of high instability while preserving fast progress in smooth basins, linking the step size directly to the estimated geometric conflict.

Using differential-inclusion analysis, the authors prove almost-sure convergence to approximate Clarke stationary points at an optimal O(1/√T) rate. Experiments on quantization-aware training and noisy small-batch learning report improvements over AdamW and Prox-SGD, with accuracy gains up to 4.54% on CIFAR-100 and 4.27% on TinyImageNet. The results connect reduced gradient oscillations with improved training outcomes in the tested non-smooth settings.
icml-2026-singularity-aware-optimization.tldr: S-Adam probes local non-smooth geometry and damps unstable updates, reducing oscillations and improving reported training accuracy.

paragraphs: Sleep-analysis models commonly assign predefined stages or events, limiting how people can describe or query sleep recordings. SleepLM connects multimodal polysomnography with natural language so that sleep physiology can support descriptions, retrieval, and interactive interpretation beyond a closed set of labels.

The authors build a multilevel caption-generation pipeline and use it to curate paired sleep and text data covering more than 100,000 hours from over 10,000 individuals. Pretraining combines three objectives: contrastive alignment connects corresponding signals and language, caption generation teaches descriptions, and signal reconstruction helps retain physiological information. Together, these objectives train both cross-modal relationships and fidelity to the recorded signals.

Experiments on real-world sleep-understanding tasks report state-of-the-art improvements in zero-shot and few-shot learning, cross-modal retrieval, and captioning. SleepLM also demonstrates language-guided event localization, targeted insight generation, and zero-shot transfer to unseen tasks. The released captioning pipeline, checkpoints, and architectures support further work on language-based access to sleep recordings and representations.
icml-2026-sleeplm-natural-language-intel.tldr: SleepLM aligns sleep recordings with language to support descriptions, retrieval, event localization, and transfer to new sleep-understanding tasks.

paragraphs: Grokking describes a training pattern in which a model fits its training data well long before it begins to generalize. This paper proves that the phenomenon can occur in classical ridge regression, using overparameterized linear models trained with gradient descent and weight decay. That setting makes the delay mathematically analyzable.

The results establish the full sequence: early overfitting, an extended period of poor generalization, and eventual arbitrarily small generalization error. The authors also derive quantitative bounds on the delay in terms of training hyperparameters. Theory and experiments show that suitable hyperparameter choices can amplify or eliminate grokking, connecting its timing to controllable aspects of training.

Beyond linear regression, experiments find that the quantitative bounds also capture grokking behavior in nonlinear neural networks. That extension is empirical, while the end-to-end proof concerns the linear setting. Together, the results suggest that grokking can arise from particular training conditions and may be avoidable through tuning, without requiring fundamental changes to the architecture or learning algorithm.
icml-2026-to-grok-grokking-provable-grok.tldr: The paper proves grokking in ridge regression and quantifies how training hyperparameters can prolong or eliminate delayed generalization.

paragraphs: Multi-agent language-model systems can face attacks that hide malicious intent in seemingly ordinary interactions. Defenses based on explicit attack language and synchronized interaction graphs can struggle when attacks are subtle or agents execute asynchronously. AcMAS instead examines internal activations within individual agents to detect malicious behavior.

The framework analyzes local reasoning states without requiring an explicit graph of agent interactions. This makes its detection mechanism robust to synchronization differences in the evaluated settings. Its activation analysis also provides signals for restoring compromised agents' functionality, offering a recovery mechanism beyond removing agents from the collaboration.

Against stealthy attacks, evaluations report an F1 score of 0.94 versus 0.72 for graph-based baselines in synchronous settings, and 0.93 versus 0.38 in asynchronous settings. The method also generalizes across the tested open-source model backbones, attack intensities, and system scales. These results support internal activation signals as a useful basis for detecting subtle compromise while maintaining the functioning of a collaborating agent system.
icml-2026-when-agents-go-rogue-activatio.tldr: AcMAS detects stealthy malicious agent behavior through internal activations and uses those signals to guide recovery.
